exclusion_detail: Lead 1g (N-(pyridin-3-yl)sulfonamide) needs at least 5 reactions from the triazolethione 2: S-alkylation to 3, NBS bromination to 4, LiOH retro-Michael to 5, N-(pyridin-3-yl)chloromethanesulfonamide 9g from 3-aminopyridine (bis-sulfonylation then NaOH mono-desulfonation, 1 or 2 steps), and the final S-alkylation 5 + 9g -> 1g. Counting 8g separately and the preparation of 2 it is 7. Also compound 2 itself is only 'prepared from 1,4-dibromonaphthalene following known procedures' with no procedure in this paper or SI.

lead.label: 1g
lead.why: The SAR exploration led to the discovery of a highly potent novel URAT1 inhibitor 1g, which was 225-fold more potent than the parent lesinurad (abstract).

notes: Every compound in the series branches from intermediate 5, which depends on 2, whose preparation is by reference only, so no compound in the paper has a fully explicit route; hence []. Shortest series members (1d: 3,4,5,1d = 4 steps from 2) still rely on 2.
